body:
Effect does an odd but necessary pattern with the unique symbol definitions:

1. An API re-export with a typedef: https://github.com/Effect-TS/effect/blob/main/packages/effect/src/Effect.ts#L81
2. An internal definition type-cast to the API type.

Effectively:

- There's a single type for both symbols -- `unique symbol` are the only nominal type in TS, they are tied to the source code declaration so you must only have one place where you define `unique symbol`.
- No non-type imports from API modules required, other code can import the symbol from `./internal`
- When you click "go-to-definition" on the symbol you get taken to the API module, that's where `unique symbol` definition is.

body:
Anything perventing you from using `Obj.AnyEntity` as the base type for all of this. 
AnyProperties isn't a great type -- its just `Record<string, any>`!

Obj.Any and Relation.Any have `[EntityKind]: Obj | Relation` forced which makes TypeScript differentiate them from any other JavasScript object. On the other had, `Record<string, any>` doesn't enforce a particular type.
